signal-teal.note: The mischief. 3.89:1 / Lc +64.2 on Warm Sheet — APCA large/secondary band, which is the role it holds. White on Signal Teal is Lc −72.8 and fine despite a 4.1:1 WCAG "fail"; black passes WCAG and is unreadable (Lc +36.8). Read APCA first.

highway-green.note: The only green trusted with text. 6.6:1 on Warm Sheet, 6.9:1 reversed under white.

mint-wash.note: The tint. Zebra striping, row bands, hover fills, code backgrounds, selection. Below the perceptual threshold on paper (Lc 0.0) — correct, it bands rows rather than carrying meaning.

mint-rule.note: The hairline. In a system with no shadows, this is the entire vocabulary of separation. Lc ~20 on paper: fine as a sheet rule, the honest weak point for interactive boundaries where WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 applies.

warm-sheet.note: The page. Slightly warm, so white cells read as paper laid on paper.

cell-white.note: The specimen ground. The colour of "something is mounted here".

deep-ink.note: Glyphs, specimens, sheet headings, emphasised values. 13.9:1 / Lc +98.2 on paper. Non-text only on a plate (Lc +15.9).

body-ink.note: Running prose, table cells, nav labels. 9.1:1 / Lc +88.9 on paper. Invisible on a Highway Green plate (Lc 0.0).

faded-ink.note: Metadata, captions, inactive controls, micro-labels. 4.8:1 / Lc +71.9 on paper. Invisible on either plate (Lc 0.0).

tally-good.note: Accuracy ≥80%, fresh roadmap steps, correct tallies. Deliberately not a brand green.

feedback-correct-bg.note: Pastel ground for an exact answer; border and text reuse Tally Good.

feedback-wrong-bg.note: Pastel ground for a wrong answer; text struck through in Tally Bad.

feedback-fuzzy-bg.note: Olive-tinted rather than green, so "almost right" is visibly neither correct nor brand.

feedback-fuzzy-user-bg.note: Ground for echoing back what the user actually typed on a tolerated near-miss.

feedback-fuzzy-user-ink.note: Text on the fuzzy echo ground.

display.purpose: Page titles in full-page prose views. Lora 500, set in Signal Teal.

headline.purpose: Section headings. Lora 500 in prose views, 600 at 1.15em in reading-tips panels.

title.purpose: Sub-headings, panel names, term-card terms. Lora 600.

body.purpose: Running prose, table cells, quiz choices. Measure capped at 640px (panels, About) or 800px (Home).

label.purpose: Uppercase micro-register: sheet section headers, stats table headings, quiz-shell tabs, badges. Makes the interface read as apparatus rather than content.

glyph.purpose: The foreign-script specimen in sheet cells. Exposed as --glyph so cells scale relative to it.

prompt.purpose: The single character or toponym under test in the quiz. The largest type in the system.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Every interactive state change in the system — hover, active, focus, colour and border shifts. Browser-default easing; no custom curve exists.

motion.name: progress
motion.purpose: Quiz progress-bar fill width. The only motion that reports data rather than state.

breakpoints.name: stack
breakpoints.purpose: The system's only media query: the two script panels go from a 1fr 1fr grid to stacked rows. Everything else scales fluidly through clamp().

components.css: .ds-sheet-section { border: 1px solid var(--c-border, #c2dccb); border-radius: var(--radius, 4px); overflow: hidden; font-size: 13px; } .ds-sheet-section > h2 { background: var(--c-sign, #006747); color: #fff; font-size: 0.8em; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; padding: 3px 8px; margin: 0; } .ds-sheet-note { margin: 0; padding: 3px 7px 2px; font-size: 0.75em; color: var(--c-label, #3e4842); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--c-border, #c2dccb); } .ds-char-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(72px, 1fr)); list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; } .ds-ruled { margin: 0 -1px -1px 0; } .ds-ruled .ds-cell { border-right: 1px solid var(--c-border, #c2dccb); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--c-border, #c2dccb); } .ds-cell { background: #fff; text-align: center; padding: 3px 4px 2px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; } .ds-glyph { font-family: 'Noto Sans Thai', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 28px; line-height: 1.15; color: var(--c-head, #242b26); } .ds-rom { font-size: 1em; color: var(--c-sign, #006747); font-weight: 600; } .ds-gloss { font-size: 0.8em; color: var(--c-muted, #67716b); line-height: 1.3; }

components.name: Character Cell
components.description: The atom of the product: specimen glyph, romanisation in Highway Green, optional gloss in Faded Ink. Borderless by default; shares hairlines with neighbours in ruled listings.
components.css: .ds-cell-solo { background: #fff; border: 1px solid var(--c-border, #c2dccb); border-radius: var(--radius, 4px); text-align: center; padding: 6px 10px 4px; display: inline-flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; font-size: 13px; } .ds-cell-glyph { font-family: 'Noto Serif', Georgia, serif; font-size: 30px; line-height: 1.15; color: var(--c-head, #242b26); } .ds-cell-rom { color: var(--c-sign, #006747); font-weight: 600; } .ds-cell-gloss { font-size: 0.8em; color: var(--c-muted, #67716b); line-height: 1.3; }

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single forward action in a view — Check, Next, Play another, Login. Signal Teal ground, no border.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { padding: 8px 20px; border: none; border-radius: var(--radius, 4px); background: var(--c-accent, #0a8f6f); color: #fff; font-size: 13px; font-family: 'Noto Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: opacity 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { opacity: 0.85; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--c-accent, #0a8f6f); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Optional actions alongside a primary — Copy results. Hairline on transparent; hover deepens ink and border rather than filling.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { padding: 8px 20px; border: 1px solid var(--c-border, #c2dccb); border-radius: var(--radius, 4px); background: transparent; color: var(--c-label, #3e4842); font-size: 13px; font-family: 'Noto Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: color 0.15s, border-color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { color: var(--c-head, #242b26); border-color: var(--c-label, #3e4842); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--c-accent, #0a8f6f); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Toolbar Pill
components.description: Quiz toolbar and stats filter control. Muted at rest, ink and border step up on hover, Mint Wash fill plus Highway Green border when active. Locked variant is a span with a title, never a disabled button.
components.html: Revision
components.css: .ds-pill-row { display: flex; gap: 4px; align-items: center; } .ds-pill { padding: 3px 10px; border: 1px solid var(--c-border, #c2dccb); border-radius: var(--radius, 4px); background: transparent; color: var(--c-muted, #67716b); font-size: 11px; font-family: 'Noto Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.15s; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-pill:hover { color: var(--c-label, #3e4842); border-color: var(--c-label, #3e4842); } .ds-pill-active { background: var(--c-alt, #e3f3ec); border-color: var(--c-sign, #006747); color: var(--c-head, #242b26); } .ds-pill-locked { opacity: 0.4; cursor: default; } .ds-pill-locked:hover { color: var(--c-muted, #67716b); border-color: var(--c-border, #c2dccb); } .ds-pill:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--c-accent, #0a8f6f); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Panel Tab Bar
components.description: The info/practice panel tab strip. Scrolls horizontally with hidden scrollbars and a mask-image fade at the right edge that signals more tabs without spending a chevron. Active tab takes the Highway Green plate.

components.name: Sidebar Nav Item

components.name: Answer Input
components.description: The type-in quiz field. Border shifts to Highway Green on focus. Browser autocomplete, autocorrect and spellcheck are all disabled — the browser must never help transliterate.

components.css: .ds-input-row { display: flex; gap: 8px; width: 100%; max-width: 360px; } .ds-input { flex: 1; padding: 8px 12px; border: 1px solid var(--c-border, #c2dccb); border-radius: var(--radius, 4px); font-size: 14px; font-family: 'Noto Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; background: #fff; color: var(--c-head, #242b26); transition: border-color 0.15s; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--c-muted, #67716b); } .ds-input:focus { border-color: var(--c-sign, #006747); outline: 2px solid var(--c-accent, #0a8f6f); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Choice Button

components.description: Marks which languages a Cyrillic letter or rule applies to. Colours come from D3 Category 20 assigned by a fixed code order, with text colour chosen per-badge by luminance. Codes are BCP-47 so the same values double as lang attributes for OpenType locl substitutions.

narrative.overview:
The system is designed as though it were an A4/A5 reference sheet on sturdy glossy stock, made by a typographer whose day job is maps, and sold in a bookshop beside bird-species posters and wall maps of places worth visiting. That single image settles most questions before they are asked. Density is not a constraint to apologise for — a handout you paid for does not waste the sheet. Nothing is at a default value, because somebody competent set this. And the sheets are an object: if a sheet could not be printed on paper and still work, it has drifted.

Its typographic lineage is textbooks, map legends, the supplementary lists tucked into a map's corner, and a little newspaper. The layout target is an engineering manual, not a magazine: condensed, tabulated, ruled. The system aims to be roughly 80–90% faithful to Matthew Butterick's Practical Typography, and the interesting part is the remaining 10–20%, where a screen and an interactive quiz demand things a printed page never had to answer.

Roadsign iconography is the flavour, not the foundation — the kind of thematic nod a print designer might reach for anyway, since textbook and map design were never uniform either. It shows up as a highway-green plate under white lettering, and only where something genuinely behaves like a plate. Everything else is the paper, the rules, and the ink.
keyCharacteristics: Condensed to engineering-manual density; whitespace is earned, never default
Mint hairlines and tonal fills do all the work that shadows would do elsewhere
The foreign glyph is the only element permitted to be large
Chrome is set at 10–13px and recedes; the sheet is the subject
A near-neutral ink with a faint green cast, so the greens read as deliberate
Print-plausible: a sheet should survive being printed on A5 and still function

rules.name: The Plate Rule
rules.body: White-on-Highway-Green is reserved for surfaces that genuinely behave like a plate: sheet section headers, the active tab, the active nav item. It is the roadsign nod, and it works because it is rationed — a handful per screen. Applied to anything that is merely selected, prominent, or in need of attention, the nod becomes a costume.

rules.name: The Neutral Ink Rule
rules.body: All three ink tones carry a faint green cast (#242b26, #3e4842, #67716b) rather than being true greys. Never substitute a pure neutral; the greens only read as deliberate because the ink quietly agrees with them.

rules.name: The ink trap
rules.body: Body Ink and Faded Ink sit almost exactly at Highway Green's luminance, so on a plate they are not merely low-contrast — they are literally invisible (Lc 0.0, WCAG 1.37:1). Faded Ink on Signal Teal is the same. An ink that reads fine everywhere on paper vanishes the moment it lands on a plate, and both contrast systems agree. Never demote plate text to an ink tone to make it look secondary; use a lighter tone instead.

rules.name: The Butterick Rule
rules.body: Target 80–90% fidelity to Practical Typography: real measure limits, no double spaces, proper dashes and quotes, restrained emphasis, purposeful line length, no decorative type. Where a screen genuinely differs from a page — interactive states, scroll, live data density — deviate on purpose and be able to say why. "It looked nicer" is not a why.

rules.name: The Specimen Rule
rules.body: The foreign glyph is the only thing allowed to be large. Every other element is set between 10px and 1.6rem. When a new element wants to be big, it is almost always trying to be the specimen — and it isn't.

rules.name: The Weight Split Rule
rules.body: Lora runs at 500 in full-page prose and 600 in panels. The larger prose sizes carry more ink per stroke, so they want the lighter weight; the compact panel sizes need the heavier one. Do not homogenise these to a single weight.

rules.name: The Shrinking Scale Rule
rules.body: Every scale in this system — type sizes, spacing steps, radii, colours — is under permanent pressure to inflate, because each individual addition looks reasonable in isolation. Treat a smaller palette as the default-correct answer: reach for an existing step before adding one, and when two steps are close enough that nobody could name the difference, they are one step.

rules.name: The Handout Density Rule
rules.body: A handout you paid for does not waste the sheet. Before adding padding, ask whether a printed reference sheet would spend that space. Usually it would not. Whitespace here is structural — it separates groups — and is not applied for comfort.

rules.name: The Print Test
rules.body: A sheet should be printable on A5 and still work. If a design depends on hover, scroll position, or viewport height to be legible, it has stopped being a handout.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Never introduce a shadow, glow, blur or gradient to signal depth, state or importance. If something needs to come forward, give it a hairline, a tonal fill, or a plate — in that order.

rules.name: The Two Registers Rule
rules.body: Chrome and quiz are set differently on purpose. Chrome — sidebar, panel tabs, toolbars, stats filters — is the fixture around the handout: restrained, near-muted, typographic, 10–13px, hairline-bordered, no fills except on hover and active. The quiz is inhabited for an uninterrupted stretch, so its controls are frankly interactive: 14px targets, real buttons with fills, coloured feedback rows, generous 2rem card padding. Both obey the same palette, radii and type families; they differ in how much presence they are allowed. Do not flatten one into the other.

rules.name: The Muted Chrome Rule
rules.body: Interface controls rest at Faded Ink and step up to Body Ink on hover. A control at full Deep Ink is either active or a bug.

dos: Do ask "would a map-shop handout do this?" before adding space, weight or colour. It answers most layout questions correctly.

Do carry the sheet's typographic conventions into every dense listing — hairline rules, Mint Wash banding, uppercase micro-label headers, tight cell padding. The sheets are the house style, not a special case. Known drift: the stats table and the reading-tips panels were built as app UI that happens to sit near sheets; moving them toward sheet conventions is a licensed improvement, not a redesign.
Do use the hairline → tonal fill → plate ladder, in that order, to express depth.
Do keep new radii to 2px or 4px.
Do spend an existing scale step before inventing one — for type, spacing, radii and colour alike. Scales only ever inflate; the smaller palette is the default-correct answer.
Do reserve white-on-Highway-Green for surfaces that genuinely act as plates.
Do let the glyph be the only large thing on screen.
Do state maturity per script with the existing beta badge and dimming, rather than hedging the whole interface.
Do deviate from Butterick when a screen genuinely demands it — and record why.
donts: Don't add a shadow, glow, blur, gradient or glassmorphic surface. Not for depth, not for state, not for emphasis.

Don't treat a WCAG 2.x ratio as the last word on Signal Teal. Check APCA before changing anything — white-on-teal is Lc −72.8 and fine, despite reading as a 4.1:1 "fail". Signal Teal as body-size text on Warm Sheet stays the weak case, but it is a guideline to weigh, not a prohibition. See "On Signal Teal" in DESIGN.md.
Don't drift toward a gamified language app: no mascots, streak flames, confetti, bouncy oversized rounded buttons, cartoon illustration or celebratory motion.
Don't drift toward a generic SaaS dashboard: no card-on-card stacking, gradient headers, purple/blue tech palette, floating widgets or comfort padding.
Don't chase trends: no neon, no heavy blur, no animated gradients, no dark-mode-first inversion of a system built as printed paper.
Don't produce undifferentiated walls of prose. Academic typography is part of the lineage; unstructured academic text is the failure mode — tabulate, rule and group instead.
Don't homogenise the two registers, or the Lora 500/600 split, in the name of consistency. Both differences are decisions.
Don't use the brand greens for status. Accuracy, freshness and correctness have their own palette so a score is never mistaken for branding.
Don't exceed one breakpoint's worth of complexity — reach for clamp() before reaching for a media query.
